chunks: 5687 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who was killed, and he had one brother in Dār al-Hijrah and another brother in Dār al-Badw who had not migrated. I said: “If the migrant pardons, and the Bedouin wants to kill, does he have that right?” He said: “The Bedouin has no right to kill a migrant until he migrates; and if the migrant pardons, then his pardon is valid.” I said to him: “Does the Bedouin have any share of the inheritance?” He said: “As for the inheritance, it belongs to him, and he has his share from the blood money of his slain brother, if the blood money is taken.”

key_terms.الْمِيرَاثُ: the inherited estate due to an heir
key_terms.دَارِ الْبَدْوِ: the land of the Bedouins; the desert-dwelling non-migrant setting
key_terms.دَارِ الْهِجْرَةِ: the land of migration; the polity or abode associated with migration
key_terms.دِيَةِ أَخِيهِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the blood money due in compensation for his slain brother
key_terms.عَفْوُهُ جَائِزٌ: his pardon is legally valid and effective

ai.seo_question: Does a non-migrant heir have the right to demand retaliation, inheritance, or blood money for a slain relative?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about retaliation, pardon, inheritance, and blood money when the slain person’s heirs differ in migration status. It states that the non-migrant Bedouin heir does not exercise the right of retaliation against a migrant, while the migrant heir’s pardon is valid; however, the Bedouin still retains his share of inheritance and of the diyyah if it is taken.
